title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
This codebook documents the data preparation, descriptive summaries, visualization, and logistic regression modeling used to examine behavioral differences between users who converted and users who did not convert on the TRI website.
The goal is to identify which engagement behaviors are most strongly associated with conversion.






Note



This document is designed as a transparent analytical appendix. It shows how the data were prepared, how variables were defined, and how the models were estimated.

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
Purpose
This section creates a simple behavioral comparison between users who converted and users who did not convert.

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
Data Source
The dataset used in this section was exported from BigQuery and saved locally as tri_logistic_clean.csv.

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
Load Data

data <- read_csv("tri_logistic_clean.csv", skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
Model 1: Behavioral Model
This model estimates the relationship between conversion and user behavior using log-transformed engagement measures plus device and traffic source controls.

model_improved <- glm(
  conversion ~ page_views_log + device_category + medium,
  data = data,
  family = "binomial"
)

    Data & SourceGoogle Analytics 4 data from TRI website. Separating the audience between converters and non-converters using BigQuery export.
    Managerial ProblemUsers were viewing TRI's site however there were not many who stayed to sign up for trainings or donations.
    Target AudienceThe Trauma Resource Institute specializes with healthcare professionals, but also anyone interested in learning more about trauma and coping.
    Research Questions / ObjectivesHow can TRI platform their website to encourage more conversions? Which channels contribute most to conversion?
    MethodsMarkov Chain attribution, Shapley value analysis, first-touch vs last-touch comparison, path length analysis using R.

    Visualizations
    

    
      Key Findings
      
        All four channels matter. Markov and Shapley models show roughly equal contribution (~20–22 credits each).
        Mobile and Paid Search are structurally essential. Removing either causes the largest drop in conversion probability (~68%).
        Social Media is undervalued by heuristics. The Markov model lifts it to near-parity (19.5 credits), suggesting an important mid-funnel role.
        Longer journeys convert better. Users with more touchpoints have higher conversion rates.
      
      Recommendation: Use the Markov model as the primary attribution framework and Shapley values as a fairness check.
